name: GPT-4o / GPT-4.1 family
summary: OpenAI's flagship multimodal model family, handling text, image, and audio input with strong general-purpose reasoning and tool-use support.
considerations: Cost scales with context length and multimodal input
Model behavior changes across dated snapshots

name: OpenAI o-series reasoning models
summary: Models tuned for extended step-by-step reasoning on hard problems (math, coding, planning), trading latency and cost for deeper reasoning.
strengths: Good fit for complex coding/math tasks
considerations: Higher latency than general-purpose chat models

name: Claude model family
summary: Anthropic's model family spanning fast/lightweight to frontier-capability tiers, with an emphasis on instruction-following, long-context handling, and constitutional-AI-based safety alignment.
considerations: Tiered model selection needed to balance cost vs. capability per task

name: Gemini model family
summary: Google's natively multimodal model family, available via the Gemini API and Vertex AI, spanning lightweight to high-capability tiers.

source.title: Gemini models overview
source.reference: Google Cloud Vertex AI documentation — Gemini models.

strengths: Tight integration with Google Cloud data services
considerations: Best-fit tier varies by latency/cost/capability trade-off

name: Azure OpenAI Service hosted models
summary: OpenAI models (GPT and o-series) hosted within a customer's Azure tenant, adding Azure identity, networking, and compliance controls around the same underlying models.
strengths: Enterprise identity (Entra ID) and private networking
considerations: Model/version availability lags slightly behind OpenAI's direct API in some regions

name: Amazon Titan and Bedrock-hosted third-party models
summary: Amazon's own Titan model family plus third-party models (Anthropic, Meta, Mistral, and others) offered through a single managed API via Amazon Bedrock.

source.title: Amazon Bedrock documentation
source.reference: AWS documentation — Amazon Bedrock model catalog.

strengths: Single API across multiple model providers
considerations: Feature/version parity with a vendor's own direct API can lag

name: Amazon Comprehend Medical
summary: A specialized natural language processing service that extracts medical conditions, medications, and clinical entities from unstructured clinical text, distinct from general-purpose LLMs.
considerations: Narrower scope than a general-purpose LLM — a complement to, not a replacement for, broader reasoning models
